title: Minimum Edges for Graph Dimension d
description: Studies the function minEdges(d) giving the minimum number of edges in a graph of dimension exactly d. Formalizes known values (d=0..5), proves structural results including a constructive simplex embedding of K_n in ℝⁿ, shows the complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity, analyzes growth rates, and introduces the deficiency function.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)
originalContributions: Axiomatization of the minEdges(d) function for graph dimension
Known values for d=0..5 including the d=4 surprise (K_{3,3} beats K₅)
Small-dimension completeness: for d≤3, K_{d+1} is optimal
Proof that d=4 is the first deviation from the complete graph pattern
Verification that d=5 returns to the complete graph pattern
Constructive simplex embedding: K_n embeds as unit distances in ℝⁿ
graphDimension(K_n) ≤ n proved constructively from simplex embedding
Complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity (conditional theorem)
Deficiency function δ(d) = C(d+1,2) - minEdges(d) with computed values
Equivalence: complete graph optimality ↔ zero deficiency (for d ≠ 4)
d=4 is the unique anomaly among d=1..5 (formally verified)
Growth rate analysis: successive differences and ratio computation
Under optimality conjecture, successive differences equal d+1
Linear lower bound from rigidity and quadratic upper bound from complete graphs

references.title: The dimension of the unit distance graph

meta.historicalContext: Erdős asked about the dimension of graphs as unit-distance graphs in Euclidean space. The minimum number of edges needed for a given dimension reveals surprising structure: K_{3,3} achieves dimension 4 with fewer edges than K₅.

sections.title: Graph Dimension
sections.summary: Defines unit distance embeddings and the graph dimension function.

sections.title: Minimum Edge Function
sections.summary: Axiomatizes minEdges(d) as the minimum edge count among graphs of dimension d.

sections.title: Structural Results
sections.summary: Proves K_{d+1} optimality for d≤3, the d=4 surprise, and d=5 matching.

sections.title: General Bounds
sections.summary: Linear lower bound d ≤ minEdges(d) and quadratic upper bound minEdges(d) ≤ C(d+1,2).

sections.title: Simplex Embedding Construction
sections.summary: Constructive proof that K_n embeds as unit distances in ℝⁿ via the (1/√2)eᵢ basis vector construction.

sections.title: Conjecture Relationships
sections.summary: Proves that the complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity. Key building block: C(d+1,2) monotonicity.

sections.title: Growth Rate Analysis
sections.summary: Successive differences and growth rates for known values. Under optimality conjecture, differences are exactly d+1.

sections.title: Deficiency Function
sections.summary: δ(d) = C(d+1,2) - minEdges(d) measures deviation from complete graph optimality. Proved: δ=0 for d≤3 and d=5, δ(4)=1.

overview.summary: Comprehensive investigation of the minimum edges function for graph dimension. Extends previous work with a constructive simplex embedding, conditional monotonicity proof, deficiency analysis, and growth rate characterization.
overview.keyIdea: The function minEdges(d) captures the trade-off between edge count and geometric dimension. The constructive simplex embedding proves K_n embeds in ℝⁿ with unit distances. The deficiency function δ(d) quantifies how much K_{d+1} differs from optimal, with d=4 as the unique known anomaly.
prerequisites: Basic real number arithmetic and casting

conclusion.summary: We significantly extend the minEdges formalization with a constructive simplex embedding (K_n in ℝⁿ), prove the complete graph optimality conjecture implies monotonicity, introduce and analyze the deficiency function, and verify d=4 is the unique anomaly for d≤5. All theorems are fully proved (no sorries).
openQuestions: Is K_{d+1} optimal for all d ≠ 4?
Can the simplex embedding be strengthened to K_n in ℝⁿ⁻¹?
